transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
My sleep has been all over the place for weeks, and I can’t seem to get back to anything like a normal schedule. I just really need some help figuring out how to get back on track.
Do you feel sleepy during the day and have trouble staying awake, or is the main problem that your sleep is happening at the wrong times even though you can sleep normally when you do go to bed?

It's honestly a mix of both, because my sleep is never normal even when I do go to bed. Some days I feel completely wiped out by midday like my body is made of lead, but other nights I'm either tossing and turning stressing about orders, or I'll sleep just three hours and wake up feeling totally energized and ready to work.
When your sleep is off, do you still usually fall asleep and wake up at the same times each day, just shifted later or earlier than normal, or is your sleep timing truly irregular from day to day?

My sleep is completely irregular from day to day, with no real pattern at all. Some nights I’m wired until four in the morning sketching designs, while other nights I crash early but wake up at three or four staring at the ceiling. Then there are times I only sleep about three hours and wake up feeling fully charged and ready to go.
When your sleep is off, do you usually still sleep for about the same total number of hours but at the wrong times, or does the amount of sleep itself change a lot from night to night?

The actual amount of sleep changes drastically from night to night. Some nights when I'm feeling really wired, I might only sleep for about three hours and wake up feeling completely energized. Other nights, I'll crash early but wake up at three or four in the morning unable to get back to sleep, so the total hours are highly unpredictable.
Do you usually sleep the same total number of hours each day but at irregular times, or does the amount of sleep itself vary a lot from night to night?

It definitely varies a lot from night to night. Like I said, some nights I'll only get about three hours of sleep and feel completely wired and ready to go. Other nights I crash early but end up waking up at three or four in the morning, unable to get back to sleep.
Do you usually feel sleepy and struggle to stay awake during the day, or do you mainly have trouble sleeping at night without significant daytime sleepiness?

It really depends on the mood swing I'm in. During my low periods, my sleep is terrible and I feel completely wiped out and heavy by midday. But during those "high" times, I only sleep about three hours and feel totally energized and wired all day without any sleepiness at all.
When your sleep is off, do you still sleep and wake at about the same times each day but shifted later or earlier than usual, or is the timing truly different from day to day with no regular pattern?

It is truly different from day to day with absolutely no regular pattern. Some nights I'm wired and awake until 4 AM sketching, while other nights I crash early but still wake up at 3 or 4 AM unable to fall back asleep. There are even times I only sleep about three hours but wake up feeling oddly energized and ready to go.
When your sleep is irregular, do you still feel sleepy and unable to stay awake during the day, or do you mainly have trouble sleeping without feeling unusually sleepy?

It completely depends on my mood at the time. On my low days, I feel totally exhausted and wiped out during the day, even after crashing early or staring at the ceiling all night. But during my "on" periods, I can sleep for just three hours and wake up feeling fully energized, with no daytime sleepiness at all.
Do these short-sleep, energized periods happen along with other symptoms of feeling unusually high or irritable, like racing thoughts, talking more, increased activity, or taking more risks?

Yes, those short-sleep periods definitely happen together with those other feelings. During those "on" times, I get oddly pumped up and snappy, talking a mile a minute while pacing around the shop and taking on way too many extra custom orders and commitments.
When you have the short-sleep periods, do you feel tired but unable to sleep, or do you actually need much less sleep and still feel energized the next day?

It actually depends on the phase I'm in. During those "on" periods, I only sleep about three hours but wake up feeling fully energized, wired, and ready to work, needing much less sleep. But at other times, like lately, I'll wake up early, stare at the ceiling stressing about orders, and feel completely exhausted and unrefreshed despite trying to sleep.
During your worst sleep periods, do you still feel sleepy and unable to stay awake during the day, or do you mainly have trouble sleeping without feeling unusually sleepy?

It really depends on which mode I'm in. During my low periods, I wake up early and can't get back to sleep, leaving me completely exhausted and wiped out during the day like my body is made of lead. But on my "on" days, I only sleep about three hours and wake up feeling totally energized and ready to work, without feeling sleepy at all.

During those 'on' periods when you need much less sleep, do you also have other symptoms like feeling unusually confident or invincible, having racing thoughts, talking more than usual, or doing risky things?

Yes, during those times I feel incredibly confident, like I'm the best jeweler in north Georgia, and I'll even brag to folks at church about how my business is about to blow up. I also talk a mile a minute and swing between joking around and getting really snappy with people. I haven't done anything physically dangerous, but I do take on way too much work and make promises I can't keep.
During your low periods, do you also lose interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or feel hopeless or worthless?

Yes, I absolutely do. I've lost interest in things I usually love, and even finishing a beautiful ring doesn't give me any spark anymore. I also keep beating myself up, feeling like a complete screw-up who ruined my business, and I constantly replay that angry client's email in my head like proof that I don't deserve people's trust.
Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days, or up to a week or more, when you felt unusually energized or irritable with much less need for sleep and the other symptoms we discussed?

Yes, I've definitely had those periods, and they've actually been going on for at least the last couple of months, especially during the busy wedding and engagement season. During those times, I'd feel incredibly energized but also really snappy, and I'd sleep only about three hours a night but still wake up feeling completely wired and ready to go.

Have you ever had a period like that where the high energy, less need for sleep, and racing or snappy mood lasted for at least 1 week and caused major problems at work, at home, or led to needing hospitalization?

Yes, those periods have been going on for at least the last couple of months, which is much longer than just a week. I haven't been hospitalized, but it has definitely caused major problems—I've missed multiple work deadlines, had a huge commission canceled, and I've started avoiding my friends from church and bluegrass jams because I'm either too keyed up or too exhausted to show up.
Have you ever had a period of at least 7 days when you felt unusually energized or irritable with much less need for sleep, and it clearly caused major problems at work, at home, or in relationships?

Yes, I've definitely had those periods last for weeks at a time over the last couple of months, where I'd get into those "on" modes, sleep only three hours, and feel completely wired while pacing around and taking on way too many projects. It also made me really snappy and irritable, which caused major problems like missing deadlines, losing a huge commission, arguing with my boss, and pulling away from my friends and church community.
Have you also had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest most of the day nearly every day, not just a few days here and there?

Yes, I've been feeling this heavy, empty sadness for about a month now, ever since things really blew up with that angry client. It sits in my chest most days, and I've completely lost interest in my work—even finishing a beautiful ring doesn't give me any spark or joy anymore.

Have you ever had a full manic episode lasting at least 1 week that was severe enough to require hospitalization or caused psychosis, such as hearing or seeing things others did not or having beliefs that were clearly not true?
No, I've never been hospitalized for any of these mood swings. I also haven't ever experienced hallucinations like hearing or seeing things, or had any severe beliefs that weren't true.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week when your mood and energy were so high or irritable that you became severely impaired, needed hospitalization, or had psychosis such as hearing or seeing things others could not?

Yes, I've had periods lasting several weeks where my energy was incredibly high, bouncy, and irritable. While I've never been hospitalized or seen or heard things that weren't there, these high periods have severely messed up my life. They caused me to lose a major client, completely ruined my workflow at the shop, and led me to avoid my friends.
Have you ever had a period of at least 7 days where you felt so unusually high, energized, or irritable that it caused major problems or made it hard to function?

Yes, I've had those periods last for weeks at a time over the last couple of months. During those times, I felt like I had endless energy, barely slept, and thought I could handle any order on my own. It definitely caused major problems, leading to missed deadlines, losing a huge custom commission, and avoiding my friends.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in most things nearly every day, separate from the high-energy periods?

Yes, I've been in a heavy, low spell for about a month now, ever since that client commission fell through. I feel this empty sadness in my chest and have lost all interest in things I usually love, like finishing a beautiful ring. This low period is completely separate and different from those high-energy phases where I'm buzzing around the shop.
Have you ever had a period of at least 7 days when you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable with much less need for sleep, even if you were not depressed at the same time?

Yes, absolutely. Before this heavy depression set in about a month ago, I had several weeks where I felt that way and wasn't depressed at all. During those "on" phases, I felt like I could conquer anything, paced around working on endless projects with only three hours of sleep, and would get easily irritated and snappy.
During your high-energy periods, did you ever become so impaired that you needed hospitalization, or did you have hallucinations or fixed beliefs that others said were not true?
No, I've never been hospitalized during those high-energy times. I also haven't experienced any hallucinations or had any unusual beliefs that others disputed.
Have you ever had a time when your mood became so high or irritable that you needed to be hospitalized, or you started hearing, seeing, or believing things that other people said were not real?
No, I have never been hospitalized because of my mood. I have also never seen, heard, or believed things that other people said weren't real.
During your low periods, have you had thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yes, when things get really bad, I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn't wake up. I've even found myself picturing driving off one of those steep curves on the way up to the trailhead. It really scares me when I think about it later, though.
Have you had any thoughts of actually harming yourself, or made any plan or taken any steps toward doing it?

No, I haven't made any plans or taken any steps to actually harm myself. I've only pictured driving off one of those steep curves on the way to the trailhead when things get really bad, but that thought actually scares me when I think about it later.
During your low periods, have you had thoughts of wanting to die or of hurting yourself, even if you would not act on them?

Yes, when it gets really bad, I do catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn't wake up. I've even pictured driving off one of those steep curves on the way to the trailhead, although those thoughts really scare me when I think about them later. I definitely wouldn't act on them, though.
During your high-energy periods, did you ever become so impaired that you needed hospitalization, or have hallucinations or fixed beliefs that others said were not real?
No, I have never been hospitalized during those high-energy times. I also haven't experienced any hallucinations or had beliefs that other people found unrealistic.
During your high-energy periods, did you ever become so impaired that you needed hospitalization, or have hallucinations or fixed beliefs that others said were not real?
No, I've never been hospitalized for those high-energy periods. I also haven't had any hallucinations or beliefs that others told me weren't real.
During your low periods, do you also have some of the 'high' symptoms at the same time, like feeling wired, talking more, racing thoughts, or needing much less sleep?

Yes, while the high and low periods usually feel like distinct phases, they can swing back and forth incredibly fast. On some days, I can go from talking a mile a minute and feeling pumped up to suddenly feeling extremely snappy, irritable, or down within the same afternoon. My sleep similarly fluctuates wildly, from being wired late at night to crashing early and waking up anxious.
